title: FlashAttention v3 startup shims, graceful degradation, and regression guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: FlashAttention v3 (FA3) offers notable throughput and memory advantages for long-sequence workloads but has produced occasional outlier latency regressions and memory edge-cases during cold startups in production. Previous mitigations (ad-hoc warmup, static kernel fallbacks) have reduced incidence but are insufficient for mixed workloads and multi-tenant Dedicated clusters. Goal: Implement a structured set of startup shims and a lightweight graceful-degradation chain to safely enable FA3 as the preferred kernel while providing deterministic, observable fallback behavior when startup or prefill scheduling risks spike latency or memory pressure. Success criteria: 1) No customer-facing latency regressions above 95th percentile during canary rollouts vs baseline; 2) Automatic fallback chain keeps error/timeout rate <= baseline + 0.5% on canaries; 3) Trackable rollout metrics (per-model kernel selection rates, fallback events, prefill latency histogram) exposed in Console; 4) New synthetic microbench catches regressions in CI with <2% false positives. Scope: - Implement 'startup shim' that applies conservative selection heuristics for first N prefill requests per process (N configurable, default 8). Shims will favor FA3 only when past probe latency & memory checks pass; otherwise prefer FA2 or generic kernel. - Add a one-shot probe mechanism: first prefill triggers a short micro-benchmark in a bounded workspace to validate FA3 path latency and workspace allocation; probe is cancellable and rate-limited. - Graceful-degradation chain: FA3 -> FA3-compat (lower workspace/tiling) -> FA2 -> generic fused-attn. Each step has deterministic reasons and metrics. - Prefill/decode scheduler adjustments: prevent aggressive batching and microbatch coalescing for processes within warmup window; introduce jittered prefill pacing to avoid correlated startup spikes on multitenant nodes. - Observability/guardrails: emit kernel_selection.reason, startup_probe.duration, fallback.reason, and memory_safety. Implement canary dashboards and automated rollback triggers (latency delta, OOM trends, error-rate regression). - CI & perf harness: add FA3 startup microbench to unit perf jobs and nightly long-sequence runs. - Rollout plan: internal canary -> opt-in customers -> 10% production -> 50% -> 100% with automatic pause/rollback heuristic. Risks and mitigations: - Probe itself adds overhead: keep fast, bounded, and rate-limited; disable probe on known low-risk models. - False positives from microbench: tune thresholds and produce aggregated baselines per-model family. - Complexity in kernel routing: keep routing logic small and heavily tested; expose logic for audits. Deliverables: - Runtime code: startup_shim + probe + fallback chain + scheduler flags. - Console metrics & canary dashboard. - CI perf tests and blocking alerts. - Design doc and runbook for oncall. Dependencies: kernel compat layers (FA2/FA3 library API stability), Console metrics ingestion, perf harness infra. Timeline: design + spec (2 weeks), implementation (3 weeks), internal canary (1 week), iterative tuning & gradual rollout (2+ weeks).

2026-03-07 - Perf results: internal canary on staging cluster (2k requests, mixed seq lengths) showed 1.2% reduction in 99th latency vs previous FA2 baseline when probe passes; 0.4% regression in tail when probe fails and fallback to FA2 occurs (within acceptable threshold). Added ticket for tuning probe thresholds (ENG-119005).

notes: This ticket focuses on engineering safety nets and observability. Work on algorithmic tiling optimizations for FA3 is tracked elsewhere and will integrate with the fallback chain once stable. Monitor Console kernel_selection.rate closely during canary and be prepared to pause rollout if fallback.rate > 5% sustained for 10 minutes.
